stories.title: 'One-positron cyclotron' could test a key prediction of the Standard Model
stories.desc: The positron is the antimatter counterpart of the electron, identical in mass but carrying an equal and opposite electric charge. Like the electron, it also behaves like a tiny bar magnet, and according to a key prediction of the Standard Model of particle physics, its magnetic moment should be…

stories.title: Counting magnetic flux quanta offers new way to measure photon numbers
stories.desc: Researchers at AIST have directly observed magnetic flux quanta generated in a superconductor by photon absorption and demonstrated a new principle of photon detection that identifies the number of photons based on the number of these flux quanta.

stories.title: Plain silicon grating reveals a hidden 'twist' in light from electron beams
stories.desc: In 1953, two physicists showed that an electron beam skimming past a grating emits light whose color depends only on the electron's speed and the grating's spacing.
